metadata.note: The Illinois Central's Omaha line: 133 miles from Tara, just outside Fort Dodge, southwest across Iowa to Council Bluffs, built by the Fort Dodge & Omaha Railroad in 1898–99 and conveyed to the IC's Dubuque & Sioux City subsidiary in 1900. It hung off the Iowa Division main line already drawn in illinois_central_iowa_division.geojson and gave the IC its own way into the Omaha gateway. Added 2026-08-27. Drawn 1900–1939, from the first through trains to the year the IC dropped passenger service to Council Bluffs.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: The 1939 end date comes from a local newspaper history saying the IC "dropped passenger service to Council Bluffs in 1939"; no discontinuance notice or last-run date was found, and whether any local train continued east of Council Bluffs after 1939 has not been checked. Every headway_min here is an estimate.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Illinois Central Railroad, Illinois Central Missouri River Bridge), Newberry Library finding aid for the Fort Dodge and Omaha Railroad Company Records, Council Bluffs Nonpareil, american-rails.com

properties.line: Illinois Central: Fort Dodge – Council Bluffs
properties.speed_source: Estimated, not sourced: a secondary line worked by local trains. No timetable was consulted.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, and about as clean as a trace on this map gets: the ways named 'CN Omaha Subdivision' that still carry old_railway_operator=IC chain into a single unbroken 130.9-mile line from Fort Dodge to Council Bluffs, used verbatim, with no gap to bridge and no shortest-path routing needed anywhere on the route. 130.9 traced miles against the 133 miles the Fort Dodge & Omaha's own records document — a close enough fit to confirm the trace is on the right railroad end to end. 0 straight-line bridges; longest raw step 1.91 km, which is ordinary tangent track across the Iowa prairie. The line is drawn to Council Bluffs and stops there: the crossing to Omaha used the East Omaha Bridge, which the IC's passenger trains used only in 1900–1921 and 1938–39, and that crossing is NOT drawn. CAVEAT (CLAUDE.md Rule 2): modern alignment drawn back to 1900. Straight-line repair 2026-08-29: 2 ruled segments totalling 31 mi replaced with OpenStreetMap-traced rail geometry (see geometry_repairs for the OSM lines each one followed).
geometry_source: OpenStreetMap ways named 'CN Omaha Subdivision' tagged old_railway_operator=IC, pulled via Overpass 2026-08-27

segments.note: The Fort Dodge & Omaha Railroad was incorporated in Iowa on 13 September 1898 and finished its 133 miles from Tara, near Fort Dodge, to Council Bluffs on 18 December 1899; the company was sold and conveyed to the Illinois Central's Dubuque & Sioux City Railroad on 22 June 1900. IC trains began running through to Omaha in January 1900, crossing on the East Omaha Bridge, and the railroad put up a two-storey brown brick depot at 12th Street and West Broadway in Council Bluffs in 1900. headway_min is an estimate, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the 13 September 1898 incorporation, the 133-mile length, the 18 December 1899 completion, the 22 June 1900 conveyance, the January 1900 start of through service and the 1900 Council Bluffs depot are carried by the references below; the headway is NOT sourced.

segments.note: IC passenger trains stopped using the East Omaha Bridge in 1921, leaving Council Bluffs as the western passenger terminal of the line. headway_min is an estimate, not read off a timetable.
sources: Segment-level: the 1921 end of passenger use of the East Omaha Bridge is carried by the references below; the headway is NOT sourced.

segments.note: IC passenger trains crossed the East Omaha Bridge again for a year, in 1938–39. The Illinois Central dropped passenger service to Council Bluffs in 1939, ending scheduled passenger service on this line; freight continued for decades and CN still runs the route as the Omaha Subdivision. headway_min is an estimate, not read off a timetable.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: the 1938–39 return to the East Omaha Bridge and the 1939 end of Council Bluffs passenger service are carried by the references below, but no last-run date was found and this segment's one-year span is inferred, not documented.
